title: Generic-point closure gives an alteration of an image stratum
statement: Let $h:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism of reduced Noetherian schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data], and let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be an integral closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-integral-scheme] whose underlying space is contained in the image of $h$. Then there are an integral closed subscheme $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$ and a morphism $a:W\to Z$ such that the composite $W\xrightarrow{a}Z\hookrightarrow X$ equals $h\circ j$, and $a$ is proper, surjective, and finite over a dense open subscheme of $Z$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular $a$ is an alteration in the sense of [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data].

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1 proof, p. 8 (author PDF lines 668--674): closure of a closed point over the generic point of Z.

proof.text: *Choose a point over the generic point with finite residue extension.* Let $\eta$ be the generic point of the integral closed subscheme $Z$. The hypothesis on the underlying image of $h$ gives a point of $Y$ over $\eta$. Let $Y_\eta=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ be the fibre of $h$ over $\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; its first projection is a homeomorphism onto the subspace $h^{-1}(\eta)$ of $Y$, so $Y_\eta$ is nonempty. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1) the projection $Y_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ is proper, in particular of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A nonempty affine open $U\subseteq Y_\eta$ is of finite type over $\kappa(\eta)$ and its coordinate ring has a maximal ideal, giving a point $z$ closed in $U$; by [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a) applied to $U$, $\kappa(z)$ is a finite extension of $\kappa(\eta)$. Let $y\in Y$ be the image of $z$, so $h(y)=\eta$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] to $z$: here $\kappa(y)\otimes_{\kappa(\eta)}\kappa(\eta)=\kappa(y)$ is a field, so the attached prime is $0$ and $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism of extensions of $\kappa(\eta)$. Hence the extension $\kappa(\eta)\to\kappa(y)$ induced by $h$ is finite. The closure of $y$ is a nonempty irreducible closed subset of $Y$ whose generic point is $y$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1 proof, p. 8 (author PDF lines 668--674): choose a closed point over the generic point and take its closure.

proof.text: *Form the integral closed subscheme and factor through $Z$.* Give the closure $\overline{\{y\}}$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Call the resulting closed immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$. It is integral: it is nonempty, reduced by construction, and irreducible because its underlying space is the closure of one point. Since every point of $W$ specializes from $y$ and $h(y)=\eta$, the underlying image of $h\circ j$ is contained in the underlying space of $Z$ (the image of a specialization is a specialization, and $Z$ is closed). The reduced-source factorization lemma [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] therefore gives a morphism $a:W\to Z$ with $i_Z\circ a=h\circ j$, where $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is the given closed immersion.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1 proof, p. 8 (author PDF lines 668--674): closure of the chosen point and its map to the closed image.

proof.text: *Properness of $a$.* The composite $h\circ j:W\to X$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], since $j$ is a closed immersion and $h$ is proper. Because $i_Z$ is a closed immersion, hence a monomorphism, the square with top map $a$ and bottom map $h\circ j$ is Cartesian: the factorization through $i_Z$ identifies $W$ with $W\times_X Z$. Thus $a$ is the base change of $h\circ j$ along $i_Z$, and is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1). The displayed equality $i_Z\circ a=h\circ j$ is the required composite identity (with the conventional order of composition read as $W\xrightarrow{a}Z\xrightarrow{i_Z}X$).

source.place: Tags 01W5 and 01W4 (closed immersions proper; properness stable under base change), applied to the closure map.

proof.text: *Finiteness on a dense open.* We show that the set-theoretic fibre $a^{-1}(\eta)$ is $\{y\}$. The closed immersions $j$ and $i_Z$ induce isomorphisms $\kappa_Y(y)\cong\kappa_W(y)$ and $\kappa_X(\eta)\cong\kappa_Z(\eta)$ of residue fields [lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-immersion](1), compatible with the maps induced by $h$ and $a$ because $i_Z\circ a=h\circ j$; so by Step 1 the extension $\kappa_Z(\eta)\to\kappa_W(y)$ induced by $a$ is finite. Let $W_\eta=W\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ be the fibre of $a$ over $\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; its first projection is a homeomorphism onto the subspace $a^{-1}(\eta)$ of $W$, and $W_\eta$ is of finite type over $\kappa(\eta)$ because $a$ is proper (Step 3) and properness is stable under base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1), [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The point of $W_\eta$ over $y$ has residue field $\kappa_W(y)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] (again $\kappa_W(y)\otimes_{\kappa(\eta)}\kappa(\eta)=\kappa_W(y)$ is a field), which is finite over $\kappa(\eta)$; so it is a closed point of $W_\eta$ by [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), and $\{y\}$ is closed in the subspace $a^{-1}(\eta)$. Now let $w\in a^{-1}(\eta)$. Since $y$ is the generic point of $W$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], $w\in\overline{\{y\}}$, so every open neighbourhood of $w$ in $W$ contains $y$; hence $w$ lies in the closure of $\{y\}$ inside $a^{-1}(\eta)$, which is $\{y\}$. Therefore $a^{-1}(\eta)=\{y\}$ is finite. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] hold for $a$: properness supplies quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and locally finite type, while $Z$ is Noetherian because it is a closed subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $X$. That lemma gives a dense open $U\subseteq Z$ containing $\eta$ such that $a^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02NW, finite generic fibre implies finiteness over a dense open; applied to $a:W	o Z$.

proof.text: *Surjectivity.* The image of the proper map $a$ is closed because proper morphisms are universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It contains $\eta$, since $a(y)=\eta$. The point $\eta$ is generic for the irreducible space $Z$, so every closed subset containing it is all of $Z$; hence $a$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 01W1 (definition-proper), together with the generic-point characterization of an integral scheme.

proof.text: *Alteration conclusion.* Steps 3--5 show that $a$ is proper and surjective and finite over the dense open $U$ of $Z$. Every irreducible component of $W$ is $W$ itself, and it dominates $Z$ because $a$ is surjective. Therefore all clauses in the definition of an alteration [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data] hold, and the constructed $a:W\to Z$ is an alteration.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1 proof, p. 8; conclusion that the closure map is proper, surjective and generically finite.

split_report.summary: Split the generic-point closure argument into six steps. The chosen closed point over the generic point has finite residue extension; its reduced closure is integral and factors through Z by the existing reduced-source lemma. Properness is obtained by identifying the factorization square as a base change, and the existing Tag 02NW generic-finite-neighbourhood lemma supplies finiteness on a dense open. The image is closed and contains the generic point, hence the map is surjective, so the alteration definition applies. No new DAG nodes were needed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the ancestor lem-trf-local-term-locality proof sentence choosing an integral closed W_Z over the generic point of each integral closed Z; concretely, the six steps implement the closure-of-a-closed-point argument described in Orgogozo Lemma 3.2.1, p. 8.

tool_uses.why: The factorization of h∘j through the given reduced closed subscheme Z uses the general reduced-source/set-theoretic-image criterion, which is not a route-specific lemma of sk-i-curve-zero.
The construction and uniqueness of the reduced induced closed subscheme on the closure of y are generic scheme geometry.
Finiteness after shrinking from a finite generic fibre is the general Tag 02NW theorem and is not supplied by the trace-formula unit.
Properness of the closure composite uses the general closed-immersion properness theorem.
Properness of a after identifying the factorization square as Cartesian uses general proper base change.
The finite residue-field extension at a closed point of a finite-type scheme over a field is a general Zariski-lemma tool.
Identifying the residue field of a point of a scheme-theoretic fibre with that of its image (Steps 1 and 4) is general scheme geometry; sk-i-curve-zero supplies no such lemma.
Residue fields are unchanged under the closed immersions W->Y and Z->X (Step 4); general scheme geometry not supplied by the trace-formula unit.

lean.statement: theorem exists_closed_image_generic_alteration {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] [IsNoetherian X] [IsReduced Y] [IsNoetherian Y] (h : Y ⟶ X) [IsProper h] (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z] (himage : Set.range i.base ⊆ Set.range h.base) : ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ Y), IsClosedImmersion j ∧ IsIntegral W ∧ ∃ (a : W ⟶ Z), a ≫ i = j ≫ h ∧ IsProper a ∧ Surjective a ∧ (∃ U : Z.Opens, Dense (U : Set Z) ∧ IsFinite (pullback.snd a U.ι)) ∧ IsAlteration a
